title: 1941 band: five saxes, Carl George, Basie arrangements, Larry Steele
summary: They add Jimmy Taylor and Johnny Starks, trumpeter Carl George, receive arrangements from Count Basie, and Larry Steele produces the shows.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah, uh-huh. So the band played through that year. And that year was not too exciting. But the next year, '41, they moved the bandstand over in the middle. We hired Jimmy Taylor on the tenor sax. You know Jimmy Taylor?
We had Jimmy Taylor on the tenor sax, we had Billy Starks' brother --
Johnny Starks on the alto sax. You and myself, and we had --
We had five saxophones. You directed most of the time.

That's right. And we had Carl George on trumpet. Carl George used to play with Stan Kenton. He's a black boy that went to school and studied under Gustave. And he played one of the most beautiful trumpets you ever

heard in your life. He played first trumpet in Stan Kenton's band for about five years, didn't he? About five years. Earl George. He played with us. We had Torran on the trombone. We had Bill Moore on the bass, Chester Lane on the piano. That was when Count Basie started giving us some arrangements, you know, and we used to rehearse arrangements. And we brought in Larry Steele to produce the shows. He came in.

And we had this boy, Bob Parrish from California, who sang -- I forget the song -- "Donkey Serenade." And of course we had Ted Smith for vocalist. The band still drew big crowds, and we made friends and Sleepy Tomlin was working with the band.
This gradually comes to me now. See, there's so much to think of, it's kind of hard to piece every year. It's kind of hard to just piece it.

Piecing that up, see. But anyway, the band was still sounding good. The band sounded good all through that year. We hired -- it was a dark boy who played tenor sax that formerly played with Fletcher Henderson. I can't think of his name. He didn't stay there long.
